countries.name: Czechia
countries.exemption: Tax-free after a 3-year holding period (time test)
countries.note: Every disposal (including crypto-to-crypto swaps) is a taxable event – keep complete records from day one.

countries.name: Slovakia
countries.exemption: No holding-period exemption; every sale or crypto-to-crypto swap is taxed
countries.filing: Annual personal tax return (type B), due 31 March
countries.note: A 7% rate and a 1-year exemption were cancelled before taking effect. A net crypto loss cannot offset other income.

countries.name: Poland
countries.note: Crypto-to-crypto swaps are not taxed – only sales for money, goods or services are. Calculate each sale’s PLN gain or loss.

countries.name: Austria
countries.exemption: Tax-free after 1 year only for crypto bought before March 2021; later purchases have no exemption
countries.filing: Annual return for gains via foreign exchanges; Austrian providers withhold the tax
countries.note: Crypto-to-crypto swaps are tax-neutral. Lending and mining are taxed on receipt; staking rewards and airdrops are taxed when sold, at zero cost.

countries.name: Germany
countries.note: Crypto-to-crypto swaps are taxable within the first year. FIFO record-keeping is critical.

countries.name: Hungary
countries.note: Documented acquisition costs are deductible – keep every invoice.

countries.name: Slovenia
countries.gainTax: No tax on private disposal gains (business trading is taxed)
countries.exemption: Private gains are not taxed; a proposed 25% tax was withdrawn in 2025
countries.filing: None for private gains; business and mining income in the annual return
countries.note: Mining is taxed as other income. Frequent trading can count as a business activity.

countries.name: Croatia
countries.filing: JOPPD form by the end of February (not the annual return)
countries.note: File JOPPD even for exempt sales. Losses offset gains only within the same year.

countries.name: Romania
countries.gainTax: 16% income tax on crypto gains (10% until 2025)
countries.note: The rate rose from 10% to 16% for gains from 2026. Gains under 200 lei per transaction are exempt up to 600 lei a year.

countries.name: Bulgaria
countries.note: Low flat rate; keep exchange statements so your records are audit-ready.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.gainTax: Box 3 wealth tax on a deemed return (about 36% of the assumed yield)
countries.note: No capital gains tax as such – you are taxed on an assumed return on your holdings. Box 3 is being reformed – check the current year’s rules.

countries.name: France
countries.gainTax: 31.4% flat tax (PFU: 12.8% income tax + 18.6% social charges, 2026)
countries.exemption: No holding-period exemption; total disposals up to €305 a year are exempt
countries.filing: Annual return with form 2086; foreign accounts on form 3916-bis
countries.note: Crypto-to-crypto swaps are not taxed: only sales for euros, goods or services are.

countries.name: Spain
countries.filing: Annual IRPF return; Modelo 721 for crypto held abroad over €50,000
countries.note: Crypto-to-crypto swaps are taxable disposals – use FIFO for identical coins.
